events.label: German and French government bond yields October 2 2026

slots.name: German 10-year yield
slots.sentence: Ten-year German Bund yields dropped 8.2 basis points to 3.451% as investors sought safety amid concerns about France.

slots.name: French 10-year yield
slots.sentence: Ten-year French government bonds also declined but by much less, falling by 1.0 basis points to 4.908%.

slots.name: yield volatility
slots.sentence: The selling turned wild on Thursday and continued Friday, with short-term French bond yields gyrating as much as 0.40 percentage points at one point over the two days, some of the biggest moves in years.

slots.name: bond market size
slots.sentence: France’s 3.5 trillion-euro government bond market is the largest in Europe thanks to years of high deficit spending.

slots.name: foreign debt ownership
slots.sentence: More than half of that money, worth $3.9 trillion, is owned by foreigners, according to MUFG.

slots.name: historical yield spread
slots.sentence: At its widest, French 10-year debt paid a yield 1.81 percentage points over equivalent bunds in November 2011, according to FactSet.

slots.name: current yield spread
slots.sentence: On Friday, the gap wasn’t far off that, at 1.55 points.

slots.name: French-German bond spread status
slots.sentence: Instead, “le spread,” traders’ shorthand for the difference in borrowing costs between France and Germany, widened dramatically, as did “lo spread,” or the extra yield on Italian government bonds over bunds.
